To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adaptive gradient methods, such as Adam, are sometimes ``too adaptive'' in training deep neural nets.

(1) adaptive gradient methods such SGD, Adam and Amsgrad can be unified into one algorithm with the partial adaptive parameter; (2) our proposed algorithm, Partially Adaptive Momentum Estimation Method (PAM), is able to achieve the best of both worlds in terms of training speed and generalization.

we propose a new adaptive momentum algorithm, called Partial adaptive momentum estimation method (PAM), which unifies SGD with Adam and Amsgrad, to close the generalizability gap of adaptive gradient method in training deep neural nets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects.
the following questions: 1) Why do adaptive gradient methods such Adam, AmsGrad, generalize worse than SGD?
the following questions: 1) Can we improve adaptive gradient methods? 2) Can we prove the convergence rate? 3) Can we generalize better?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adaptive gradient methods, such as Adam/Amsgard, can generalize as well as SGD with momentum if we use the right learning rate schedule and momentum.
adaptive gradient methods, if properly designed, could be as good as SGD with momentum in terms of convergence rate and generalization.
the generalization gap between SGD with momentum and adaptive gradient methods can be closed by partially adaptive momentum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the generalization performance of adaptive gradient methods could be improved by a partial adaptive momentum estimation.
we propose to partially adapt the momentum estimation method in adaptive gradient methods, which can achieve the best from adaptive gradient and SGD methods.
adaptive gradient methods are not necessarily bad for generalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the momentum estimation in adaptive gradient methods can be partially adaptive.
we should not blindly trust adaptive gradient methods, and we should always keep a balance between adaptive and SGD momentum.
we can use adaptive gradient methods to accelerate the training process of deep neural networks, while keeping their generalization ability as well as SGD.
